name: Mr. Peanut
text: Planters trademark contest: the anthropomorphic peanut character is created.

name: Mr. Peanut
text: Planters marks Mr. Peanut's 'death' in a January 2020 campaign.

name: Miss Chiquita (banana form)
text: Miss Chiquita appears as an anthropomorphic banana in Chiquita's radio advertising and animated mascot work.

name: Miss Chiquita (banana form)
text: The banana form is replaced: Miss Chiquita is redrawn as a human woman, no longer a fruit with a face.

name: Red M&M
text: Red M&M appears in M&M's television advertising.

name: Red M&M
text: The early M&M's candy figures are reworked with distinct personalities.

name: Yellow M&M
text: Yellow M&M appears in M&M's television advertising.

name: Yellow M&M
text: The peanut candy character gains a recognizable comedic personality in the 1995 M&M's relaunch.

name: Pillsbury Doughboy (Poppin’ Fresh)
text: Pillsbury Doughboy debuts in a stop-motion television commercial: a dough figure emerging from a refrigerated dough can.

name: Mayor McCheese
text: McDonaldland introduces a cheeseburger-headed figure as the mayor.

name: Officer Big Mac
text: McDonaldland introduces a burger-headed figure as the police officer.

name: Twinkie the Kid
text: Hostess presents a cream-filled snack cake as a Western cowboy.

name: Anpanman
text: Takashi Yanase's picture book introduces Anpanman, a red-bean bun hero who shares his face with the hungry.

name: Anpanman
text: Anpanman first airs as a TV anime (official chronology).

name: Currypanman
text: First TV appearance recorded in the official chronology (October 1988).

name: Shokupanman
text: First TV appearance recorded in the official chronology (1988).

name: Omusubiman
text: Appears in the official 1988 TV chronology.

name: Tendonman
text: Appears in the first TV episode of Anpanman in 1988.

name: Hamburger Kid
text: First appears on TV in May 1989.

name: Katsudonman
text: First appears on TV with Kamameshidon in July 1989.

name: Kamameshidon
text: Belongs to the Donburiman trio introduced on TV in 1989.

name: Melonpanna
text: Joins the TV cast in September 1992.

name: Bob the Tomato
text: Bob appears in a screen test; he hosts the first VeggieTales video in 1993.

name: Larry the Cucumber
text: Larry appears in a screen test and becomes VeggieTales co-host in 1993.

name: Junior Asparagus
text: Junior appears in the first VeggieTales release, in a story about fear.

name: Rollpanna
text: The official chronology records her creation, with both good and evil hearts, in 1994.

name: Frankencelery
text: A celery monster appears in the scary film Junior Asparagus watches in the first VeggieTales release.

name: Laura Carrot
text: Her official profile lists Are You My Neighbor? as her first appearance.

name: Blue M&M
text: A public vote selects the new blue candy colour, which is developed into a character.

name: Green M&M
text: Green M&M appears in television / Super Bowl advertising.

name: Green M&M
text: A redesign of her footwear becomes a widely discussed brand controversy.

name: Madame Blueberry
text: Madame Blueberry is used in a VeggieTales story about greed and gratitude.

name: Cream Panda
text: Arrives from Custard Country on TV in April 1998.

name: Yakisobapanman
text: Makes a documented TV debut in January 1999.

name: Orange M&M
text: The anxious Orange character promotes Crispy M&M's around its US launch.

name: Kogepan
text: Miki Takahashi first draws Kogepan at San-X: a burnt red-bean bun that could not be sold.

name: Kogepan
text: Kogepan stationery launches.

name: Kireipan
text: Kireipan, a well-baked and energetic bun, appears in a Kogepan picture book as a contrast to Kogepan.

name: Bad Apple
text: Apple Jacks advertising features Bad Apple, a scheming apple villain.

name: Bad Apple
text: Nutrition advocacy groups challenge the ads (CSPI letter, 2005).

name: Bad Apple
text: The campaign is discontinued by 2006.

name: CinnaMon
text: The friendly cinnamon stick faces Bad Apple in Apple Jacks advertising.

name: CinnaMon
text: The original ad campaign is discontinued by 2006.

name: Petunia Rhubarb
text: Debuts in Duke and the Great Pie War, with a story about self-worth.

name: GingerBrave
text: A gingerbread cookie escaping the witch's oven appears in the mobile game OvenBreak and launches the Cookie Run franchise.

name: Annoying Orange
text: The talking-orange videos spread on YouTube.

name: GingerDozer
text: Listed in the Cookie Run release chronology in November 2011.

name: Tonkatsu
text: A pork cutlet end piece, left uneaten because it is mostly fat, joins the Sumikkogurashi cast.

name: Strawberry Cookie
text: Listed among the 2012 Cookie Run game releases (OvenBreak 2).

name: GingerBright
text: Appears in the 2012 OvenBreak 2 character roster.

name: Ms. Brown M&M
text: Debuts at the Super Bowl in television advertising as a businesslike female candy character.

name: Gudetama
text: Sanrio debuts the lethargic egg character.

name: KIRIMI-chan.
text: Sanrio debuts a salmon slice that wishes to be eaten deliciously.

name: Frank (Sausage Party)
text: A sausage discovers the fate of supermarket food in the animated film Sausage Party.

name: Brenda Bun (Sausage Party)
text: An anthropomorphic bun is one of the supermarket characters in Sausage Party.

name: Purple M&M
text: Mars introduces Purple as a new spokescandy associated with acceptance.

name: Frosted Strawberry Pop-Tart (Bowl mascot)
text: The Pop-Tarts Bowl edible-mascot campaign: a pastry character descends into a toaster.

name: Frosted Strawberry Pop-Tart (Bowl mascot)
text: Revived in 2024 marketing.
